blocks.orig: Usambara is a beautiful mountain range with grassy plains and virgin tropical rainforest. The area has many colorful villages you can visit during your stay here. The Usambara mountains are located northeastern Tanzania, near Mkomazi National Park, about 3 hours’ drive (110 km) west of Tanga.
blocks.html: The Usambara range is a lovely mountain area of grassy plains and untouched tropical rainforest, dotted with colourful villages that you can explore while you are here. You will find the Usambara mountains in the north-east of Tanzania, close to Mkomazi National Park and roughly a 3-hour drive (110 km) west of Tanga.

blocks.orig: It is one of the undiscovered places in Tanzania. And this is what makes it a true paradise for nature and hiking lovers. The lush green mountains have a cool climate that is ideal for walks and hikes. But one of the best reasons to hike the Usambara mountains is the amazing view. You’ll see sweeping hills, mountains, valleys, farmland, picturesque villages, colourful markets and plantations everywheer you go.
blocks.html: This is still one of Tanzania’s undiscovered corners, and that is precisely what makes it such a paradise for walkers and nature lovers. The green, lush mountains enjoy a cool climate that suits walking and hiking perfectly. Yet the strongest argument for hiking in the Usambaras is the view: wherever you go, you look out over rolling hills, mountains, valleys, farmland, pretty villages, colourful markets and plantations.

blocks.orig: The Usambara mountains comprise the easternmost ranges of the Eastern Arc Mountains. They are 90 km long and about half that wide. Faulting and uplifting formed them nearly two million years ago, and they are composed of Precambrian metamorphic rocks.
blocks.html: The Usambara mountains form the easternmost ranges of the Eastern Arc Mountains. The range stretches 90 km in length and is roughly half as wide. It was created by faulting and uplift almost two million years ago and consists of Precambrian metamorphic rock.

blocks.orig: Usambara Mountains are very unusual in East Africa with their natural regions still covered in tropical forests and therefore they are considered a tremendously significant ecologically and a biodiversity hotspot with many protected zones. Several species are living in the Usambara forests, including the Usambara eagle-owl, the Usambara akalat, the Usambara weaver and the African violet. You can also spot other bird like the Mountain buzzard, Crown eagle, Eastern bronze-naped pigeon, Lemon and Dusky turtle dove and the Hartlaub’s Turaco.
blocks.html: Within East Africa the Usambara Mountains are quite exceptional, as their natural areas are still clad in tropical forest. That makes them ecologically hugely important and a recognised biodiversity hotspot with numerous protected zones. The Usambara forests are home to a range of species, among them the Usambara eagle-owl, the Usambara akalat, the Usambara weaver and the African violet. Other birds you may spot include the Mountain buzzard, Crown eagle, Eastern bronze-naped pigeon, Lemon and Dusky turtle dove and the Hartlaub’s Turaco.

blocks.orig: Flora and Fauna found in the Usambara mountains
blocks.html: Plants and wildlife of the Usambara mountains

blocks.orig: You can find over 3000 plant species and over 600 tree species that thrive in the Usambara mountains. Therefore it is rknown as one of the world’s biodiversity hotspots. It herefore attracts naturalists and nature lovers from all over the world who come to watch birds, study trees and flowers or butterflies. Several species are endemic to the Usambara forests.
blocks.html: More than 3000 plant species and over 600 tree species flourish in the Usambara mountains, which is why the area counts as one of the world’s biodiversity hotspots. Naturalists and nature enthusiasts travel here from across the globe to watch birds, study trees and flowers, or look for butterflies. A number of species occur only in the Usambara forests.

blocks.orig: You can go for a hike with a local guide and discover the beautiful diversity of this vast area. On a clear day you can see the grass plains of Mkomazi as well as Kilimanjaro and enjoy the beautiful views that this area has to offer. During this special walk you will have the opportunity to meet the locals who will wave to you and give you a friendly smile. The locals are very hospitable and if you are open and interested, you will be spontaneously invited to get to know them better.
blocks.html: Join a local guide for a hike and discover the wonderful variety of this huge area. When the sky is clear you can make out the grass plains of Mkomazi and even Kilimanjaro, while taking in the lovely views the region offers. Along the way you will meet local people who wave and greet you with a warm smile. They are very welcoming, and if you show openness and interest you may well find yourself spontaneously invited to get to know them better.

blocks.orig: You can hike up the Irente viewpoint to get a panoramic view of Mazinde village almost 1000 m below and the vast Maasai plains beyond.
blocks.html: A climb to the Irente viewpoint rewards you with a panorama over Mazinde village nearly 1000 m below and the wide Maasai plains stretching beyond it.

blocks.orig: Or walk through the fertile farmlands of Jaegertal to a fruit tree nursery and learn more about the different varieties of fruit trees and their propagation. The “Growing Rock” tour starts from Soni where you walk to the top of the Kwamongo mountain, famous for its butterflies and enjoy views of Soni, Lushoto and the Handeni plains from the peak.
blocks.html: Alternatively, walk through the fertile farmland of Jaegertal to a fruit tree nursery, where you learn about the various kinds of fruit trees and how they are propagated. The “Growing Rock” tour sets off from Soni and takes you to the summit of Kwamongo mountain, known for its butterflies, with views from the top over Soni, Lushoto and the Handeni plains.

blocks.html: Expert travel tips for the Usambara Mountains

blocks.orig: My name is Kennedy and I am a mountain guide at Usambara Mountains for 11 years. Our guests come here for hiking in the untouched forest and are always impressed with the stunning views you can along the way.
blocks.html: I am Kennedy, and I have worked as a mountain guide in the Usambara Mountains for 11 years. Guests come to us to hike through the untouched forest, and the stunning views along the route never fail to impress them.

blocks.orig: Although the climate is comfortable year-round, paths get too muddy for trekking during the rainy season from March through May. The best time to visit is from June to October, after the rains and when the air is clearest.
blocks.html: The climate is pleasant all year, but in the rainy season from March through May the trails become too muddy for trekking. June to October is the best period to come, once the rains have passed and the air is at its clearest.

blocks.orig: Usambara is a beautiful mountain range with stunning views over the grassy plains and virgin tropical rainforest and is known for the many colorful villages. It is one of the undiscovered places and makes it a true paradise for nature and hiking lovers.
blocks.html: Usambara is a lovely mountain range with magnificent views over grassy plains and untouched tropical rainforest, well known for its many colourful villages. As one of Tanzania’s undiscovered places, it is a genuine paradise for anyone who loves nature and hiking.
